key_cases.case_name: People in Interest of S.N. v. S.N.
key_cases.holding: The court held that whether a child is dependent and neglected because of prospective harm is a mixed question of law and fact, so summary judgment in such adjudications is neither always available nor always barred and must be evaluated case by case on whether the material evidentiary facts are undisputed.
key_cases.relevance: A parent contesting an adjudication has the right to a factual hearing unless the material evidentiary facts are genuinely undisputed, which is the route to dismissal at this node.
key_cases.quote: We hold that courts must evaluate whether summary judgment is appropriate in a dependency and neglect adjudication involving prospective harm on a case-by-case basis.

key_cases.holding: The court held that neither the injurious-environment provision of section 19-3-102(1)(c) nor Troxel requires the State to prove parental fault, or to prove that both parents lack the availability, ability and willingness to provide reasonable parental care, before a child may be adjudicated dependent or neglected.
key_cases.relevance: It marks the boundary of the adjudication: a case is not dismissible merely because one parent is fit or because no parent is at fault.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the statute does not require the jury to make findings of parental fault

key_cases.holding: The court held that section 19-1-109(1) authorizes an appeal from any final order in a dependency or neglect proceeding, that subsection (2) adds to rather than limits that right, and that C.A.R. 3.4(a) cannot narrow the categories of orders the statute makes appealable.
key_cases.relevance: An order dismissing a respondent or the petition is reviewable if final.
key_cases.quote: we hold that section 19-1-109(1) authorizes the appeal of any order from a dependency or neglect proceeding that is "final"
